body:
Note that Angular Material itself is defining this grey background colour. It is set deep inside the theming part of the SASS code in their library: https://github.com/angular/material2/blob/abc3d38c57146443c848d5ba26fd2fab8ca185d6/src/lib/core/theming/_palette.scss#L677

We should talk to someone... @jelbourn(?) ... about the choice of this colour and how best to override it?

Also, according to the spec ([Color theme creation][1] > `Surface, background, and error colors`):

> The background color appears behind scrollable content. The baseline background and surface color is #FFFFFF.

[1]: https://material.io/design/color/the-color-system.html#color-theme-creation

As @gkalpak said, the color is defined by the Material Design specification. 

Is there text somewhere on the site that's not meeting W3C guidelines? The tool http://contrast-ratio.com can tell you pretty easily.

I checked: http://contrast-ratio.com/#rbga%280%2C0%2C0%2C.87%29-on-%23fafafa

The current colors meet W3C AAA for any size text.
Um, @jelbourn: I think @gkalpak was saying that background and surface baseline colours are white? I note that mat-card backgrounds, are in fact white.

body: Ah, it looks like that's been changed in the 2018 update. The pre-I/O version was `#fafafa` for app background with the pure white reserved for "sheets of material" like cards and dialogs.

I'm not surprised that technically it meets accessibility standards. Every site I've worked on with this gray did, and it didn't stop readers from complaining that text blurs into background a little so they wanted a higher contrast option.

So...if I understand your point @jelbourn, the light gray background makes sense when you have cards and other elements that you want to offset...is that the idea? I can see how it pops nicely there. 

The tricky part of a text-rich site is that we want the main body to as readable as possible. Same reason the cards have white background. 

As @gkalpak pointed out in another thread, with a white background for the whole page, we do lose the ability to offset code regions or images with white card-like boxes. I'm not sure, however, that those elements are so much more important than the main text that they deserve special offset the way navigation cards are offset. But I definitely wouldn't want to offset code or images by giving them a darker background than the main page, because that definitely moves us into readability challenges. 

Hmmm....
